comments: THE 168 THEOREM — Computational Verification
Enumerate all ordered triples (i,j,k) of distinct imaginary
octonion basis elements (i,j,k ∈ {1..7}, all different).

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `ode_rk4_general`. General-Purpose RK4 ODE Solver Tests Tests a classical 4th-order Runge-Kutta integrator on four canonical ODEs: 1. Exponential decay:   du/dt = -k*u. It should compile and run successfully.
description: General-Purpose RK4 ODE Solver Tests Tests a classical 4th-order Runge-Kutta integrator on four canonical ODEs: 1. Exponential decay:   du/dt = -k*u
comments: General-Purpose RK4 ODE Solver Tests
Tests a classical 4th-order Runge-Kutta integrator on four canonical ODEs:
1. Exponential decay:   du/dt = -k*u
2. Harmonic oscillator: dx/dt = v, dv/dt = -omega^2*x
3. Logistic growth:     du/dt = r*u*(1 - u/K)
4. Stiff linear decay:  du/dt = -50*u
Plus trivial ODEs (zero RHS, constant RHS) and convergence order verification.
All functions inlined since tests cannot import.
References:
Hairer, Norsett, Wanner (1993) "Solving ODEs I: Nonstiff Problems"
Butcher (2008) "Numerical Methods for ODEs"

single function, with variance propagated through a chain of function
calls that each emit multiple variance_addsub / variance_muldiv ops.
Current status (2026-04-12): this test PASSES on the current compiler
because the slot threshold isn't hit with the minimal pattern below —

comments: Struct-field Knowledge<T> — β¹⁰ compile-fail (type mismatch on construction).
Before this fix, `scan_type()` sets SCAN_TY=0 for Knowledge<T> fields, so the
struct-literal type-check guard `if fty != 0` was never entered — any value
could be stored in a Knowledge<T> field without error.
After the fix: the guard is extended to `(fty != 0 || knowledge_hash_is(fhash))`,
so Knowledge fields are also checked via ty_eq, which returns false when the
initializer is a plain f64 (EXPR_TY==2) stored into a Knowledge<f64> field.

instruction: Write a Sounio compile-fail example named `refinement_subtype_strict`. refinement_subtype_strict The pattern used to read E001, which this program never emits — it is rejected by the refinement checker with an uncoded diagnostic. The harness was not. It should fail to compile. The compiler output should include: refinement type violation.
description: refinement_subtype_strict The pattern used to read E001, which this program never emits — it is rejected by the refinement checker with an uncoded diagnostic. The harness was not
comments: refinement_subtype_strict
The pattern used to read E001, which this program never emits — it is rejected
by the refinement checker with an uncoded diagnostic. The harness was not
matching error-pattern at all, so the test passed while asserting the wrong
thing; with the matcher fixed the annotation had to say what is actually
emitted.
`requires: lean_single` because the diagnostic this asserts is an engine
difference, not a language rule. Measured 2026-09-03 on both:
lean_single  error[E208]: refinement type violation — value 0 does not
satisfy parameter predicate at line 19        ← what is asserted
Madaros      error[E008] return value does not match declared return type
error[E001] this binding expects a different type
error[E009] argument type does not match parameter
Madaros is not missing the diagnostic — check.sio carries code 42, "value does
not satisfy the refinement predicate". It never reaches it, because it relates
a refinement type to its base type in NEITHER direction:
fn f(x: Positive) -> i32 { x }    E008, though every Positive IS an i32
let p: Positive = 0               E001, a bare type mismatch standing where
the predicate should have spoken
So the three errors above are all one gap wearing three codes, and the E009 at
the call site rejects for the wrong reason: NonNeg and Positive differ as
NAMES, not because 0 fails `n > 0`. Two identical refinement names with a
violated predicate would slip through it.
Erasure (Positive → i32) would be sound to open on its own. The introduction
direction is where the predicate must actually be evaluated, and opening it
without first proving the check fires would turn a wrongly-coded rejection
into an acceptance — a fail-open in a type system. Left for whoever implements
refinement subsumption in the modular checker, rather than half-done here.

description: Dissertation contribution #2 (compile-time confidence gate) — REFUSE path. `prescribe_tac` is annotated `with Confidence(800)`. The body must carry compile-time confidence ≥ 800/1000 on every expression token.
comments: Dissertation contribution #2 (compile-time confidence gate) — REFUSE path.
`prescribe_tac` is annotated `with Confidence(800)`. The body must carry
compile-time confidence ≥ 800/1000 on every expression token.
`measure(8.0, uncertainty: 4.0)` yields confidence = 1 − 4.0/8.0 = 0.5
= 500/1000, BELOW the 800 threshold. The compiler is required to
REJECT this program — no binary is emitted, the rejection is enforced
before any runtime check would run. Diagnostic from
lean_single.sio:20984-21006 prints
`error: EpistemicComplete violation in fn main ... (conf=500 < 800)`.
Clinical narrative: pre-TDM (n=0 samples), the only available C24h
estimate is the wide popPK prior with CV ≥ 50%. The compile-time
